options.label: C

passage.title: Comprehension passage
passage.body:
When the rains failed for the second year running, the farmers of Ikeji did not wait for help from the capital. They pooled their savings and dug a shallow reservoir at the edge of the village, lining it with clay from the riverbank. The older men doubted that such a small pond could make any difference, but the young women who organised the work kept careful records of every naira spent and every bucket of water drawn.

By the next dry season the reservoir was keeping three hectares of vegetables alive. Traders who had once driven past Ikeji now stopped to buy tomatoes and peppers. The doubters, it is said, were the first to ask for a larger reservoir.
passage.source: Kwado original (JAMB-style practice, not an official past question)

The older men doubted that such a small pond could make any difference, but the young women who organised the work kept careful records of every naira spent and every bucket of water drawn.

By the next dry season the reservoir was keeping three hectares of vegetables alive. Traders who had once driven past Ikeji now stopped to buy tomatoes and peppers. The doubters, it is said, were the first to ask for a larger reservoir.
